function: Prompted LLM (GPT-4) as search operator in a decomposition-based GWO for precoder, user/target distance and angle, trading communication rate against sensing CRB in near-field ISAC (pp. 6-9).
system: BS with N-antenna ULA, K single-antenna users or targets, near-field, no RIS; N, K and carrier frequency not stated in results; bandwidth 51.2 MHz (pp. 3, 10).
method: Pretrained GPT-4 used in-context as black-box reproduction operator inside decomposition-based (weighted Tchebycheff) multi-objective GWO; fixed prompt, lens-imaging reverse learning; no training or fine-tuning (pp. 7-9, 11).
data_channel: Custom near-field spherical-wave channel (Fresnel approximation, constant gain, free-space path loss, -60 dB at 1 m, RCS in [0.8, 1]); no dataset or measurements (pp. 4, 5, 10).
test_conditions: Single simulated setting (RCS, power limits 0-20 dBm); no training stage since the LLM is not trained; fitness tracked over 1000 iterations; no new condition tested (pp. 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: conventional GWO and MOEA/D [41]. Learned: LEDMA [40], an existing LLM-enabled metaheuristic that shares the algorithmic foundation of the proposed scheme (p. 10).
metrics: Average fitness (weighted Tchebycheff aggregation) versus iterations, Pareto front of communication rate versus log-CRB sensing objective, and radar beampattern power at targets (pp. 11-12).
complexity: O(M^2 + T(M Cf + M D + M no + M|Phi|)) over T iterations, LLM treated as black box; no runtime reported (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 4: "the channel gain of each link between the antenna elements and the user or target remains approximately identical" (eqs. 11-17 give a custom spherical-wave model with Fresnel approximation); p. 10: "The channel power at a reference distance of 1 m" is set to -60 dB. Not met: no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "The LLM does not perform online training or parameter updates"; p. 10: "the prediction performance of the proposed is evaluated with the near-field communication setting of ISAC network". Not met: no trained model, and the results use one simulated setting with no unseen scenario, configuration or adaptation.
q3_support: p. 10: "existing LLM-enabled metaheuristic algorithm, named as LEDMA [40], GWO, MOEA/D [41] and our proposed LLM-GWO framework" (non-learned GWO and MOEA/D, learned LLM-based LEDMA); p. 11: "the lowest average fitness function value of 0.007", with "the LEDMA and GWO achieve average fitness function value of 0.267 and 0.029, respectively"; p. 12: "the proposed LLM-GWO approach provides higher power at the target locations than the LEDMA and GWO-based methods".
q4_support: p. 10: "the overall computational complexity of Algorithm 1 over T iterations can be summarized as" O(M^2 + T(M Cf + M D + M no + M|Phi|)), with the LLM treated as a black-box oracle.
q5_support: p. 10: "the prediction performance of the proposed is evaluated with the near-field communication setting of ISAC network". Not met: a custom simulated setting; no code or data link, no public channel dataset and no measured data appear in the 13 pages, and GPT-4 is used through prompts only (p. 11).
notes: Included with a doubt on no_learning: the method is a metaheuristic, LLM-assisted multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (p. 9) whose reproduction operator is a prompted GPT-4 that "does not perform online training or parameter updates" (p. 9), so the only learned element is a pretrained LLM used in context; if the reviewer reads this as no learned component performing the physical-layer function, the work should be excluded as no_learning. Area 5 because problem (31) jointly optimizes a communication rate and a sensing CRB with the precoder (pp. 5-6, 9), although the variables also include the distance and angle of users and targets (p. 6) and the abstract speaks of angle and distance prediction (p. 1). ris=0: no RIS in the system model. q1=0: custom spherical-wave channel with constant gain (p. 4). q2=0: no trained model and one setting. q3=1: GWO and MOEA/D are non-learned, LEDMA [40] is an earlier LLM-based method, and the comparison is on fitness and beampattern power, not only on convergence (pp. 11-12). q4=1: the order of complexity is stated (p. 10). q5=0: no code or data link. Figs. 4-7 were read as page images: Fig. 4 shows benchmark function surfaces (r, theta, f) and p. 2 mentions an established benchmark; the results section does not state N, K or the carrier frequency (28 GHz appears only as an example on p. 4).
